desc: Prove cut-cover criterion: final graph is strongly connected iff for every k=1..2N-1 some matched pair (w,b) has b≤k<w (chain gives forward reachability; backward edges are the only way left).

Permutation formulation: q_j = white-rank matched to black-rank j; cut k ⟺ constraint max_{j≤c(k)} q_j ≥ a(k)+1; per black-rank c keep strongest RHS A_c+1 where A_c = max #whites in a prefix with exactly c blacks (k≤2N-1).

Reduce to distinct active thresholds (v_i,u_i) = (c, A_c) with A_c≥c, strictly increasing; counting recurrence derived and hand-verified on N≤3 cases, sample 1, and multi-constraint cases (incl. leakage case u_i≥v_{i+1}).
Implement reduction + O(r²) DP; validate vs brute-force SCC enumeration for N≤7 and all 3 samples (BWBW→1, BWWBWBWB→0, sample 3→240792).
Edge cases: leading W → 0 and trailing B → 0 handled by early return; A_c=N for c<N implies trailing B (covered); no active constraints → N!; A_c computed only over proper prefixes k=1..2N-1.

Cross-validate CDQ+NTT large-r path vs O(r²) DP on identical inputs with r>2000 (forced threshold off/on; randomized alternating, long-run, near-Dyck strings; no mismatches; threshold restored to 2000).

Final performance pass at N=2×10^5: worst-case alternating-ish shape timed for the full program during cross-validation; recursion limit set, NTT sizes bounded by 3N+3, I/O and mod arithmetic verified.
